questions.learningObjective: Identify the passive construction in a handover note

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «Las camas fueron revisadas por el auxiliar.» Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: El indicio de este ítem es «Identify the passive construction in a handover note / Look for ser followed by a participle. / Passives and impersonals in a text». ¿qué opción lo cumple?

options.text: Se revisaron las camas antes del turno de noche.
options.misconception: confuses the passive se with an impersonal se

options.text: El doctor revisó las camas antes del turno.
options.misconception: mistakes an active clause for a passive one

options.text: Las camas fueron revisadas por el auxiliar.
Revisaron las camas antes del turno de noche.
options.misconception: treats a plural verb without subject as passive

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: a true passive needs ser plus a past participle and an optional agent. On that basis "Las camas fueron revisadas por el auxiliar" is the supported choice. Option A ("Se revisaron las camas antes del turno de noche") fails because it confuses the passive se with an impersonal se; Option B ("El doctor revisó las camas antes del turno") fails because it mistakes an active clause for a passive one; Option D ("Revisaron las camas antes del turno de noche") fails because it treats a plural verb without subject as passive.
questions.hint: Look for ser followed by a participle.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a passive se is preferred in a handover

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «The passive se is shorter and keeps the focus on the action, not on who gave the dose, which suits a quick handover note where the agent is obvious.» « Se administró la medicación » La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: Con «Explain why a passive se is preferred in a handover / Think about brevity and focus in handover writing. / Choosing between two…» presente, ¿qué respuesta se desprende de la nota?

answer.exemplar: The passive se is shorter and keeps the focus on the action, not on who gave the dose, which suits a quick handover note where the agent is obvious.

questions.explanation: The passive se foregrounds the action and omits the agent naturally. A ser passive would add an unnecessary agent phrase and slow the note down.
questions.hint: Think about brevity and focus in handover writing.

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «La supervisora hizo llamar al cirujano.» Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: Con «Identify causative in a handover / Find hacer followed by an infinitive. / Causative constructions» presente, ¿qué respuesta se desprende de la nota?

options.text: La supervisora hizo llamar al cirujano.
Se operó al paciente.
Se cerró la herida.
Todas son causativas.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: only the first clause uses hacer plus an infinitive, showing the supervisor caused the call. On that basis "La supervisora hizo llamar al cirujano" is the supported choice. Option B ("Se operó al paciente") fails because it mistakes passive se for causative; Option C ("Se cerró la herida") fails because it confuses passive se with causative; Option D ("Todas son causativas") fails because it overgeneralises the causative reading.
questions.hint: Find hacer followed by an infinitive.

options.text: Se revisaron las camas.
Las camas fueron revisadas.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Classify a se sentence

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «Accidental se, because the indirect object marks the affected person.» « Se me rompió el vaso » Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: Aplicando «Classify a se sentence / Look for an indirect object pronoun marking the affected person. / The three constructions with se» al texto, ¿cuál de las opciones se sostiene?

options.text: Accidental se, because the indirect object marks the affected person.
Passive se, because the verb agrees with el vaso.
Impersonal se, because no agent is named.
Causative, because someone broke it.
options.misconception: selects "Causative, because someone broke it" where the rule in the passage requires a different condition

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: se me rompió' marks an unintended breaking, with the indirect object pronoun showing who was affected. On that basis "Accidental se, because the indirect object marks the affected person" is the supported choice. Option B ("Passive se, because the verb agrees with el vaso") fails because it confuses agreement with passivity; Option C ("Impersonal se, because no agent is named") fails because it overuses the no-agent test; Option D ("Causative, because someone broke it") fails because it selects "Causative, because someone broke it" where the three constructions with se requires a different condition.
questions.hint: Look for an indirect object pronoun marking the affected person.

questions.learningObjective: Decide between ser and se passive

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. «Se administró la dosis.» Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: El indicio de este ítem es «Decide between ser and se passive / Prefer passive se when the agent is irrelevant. / Choosing between two passives». ¿qué opción lo cumple?

options.text: La dosis fue administrada por la enfermera.
options.misconception: names the agent when it is unnecessary

options.text: Se administró la dosis.
La dosis se administró por la enfermera.
Administró la dosis.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: when the agent is unnecessary, passive se is concise and natural. On that basis "Se administró la dosis" is the supported choice. questions.hint: Prefer passive se when the agent is irrelevant.
